intro: Frankfurt rewards visitors with a compact old town, world-class museums and a lively riverfront. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: U-Bahn (metro), trams and buses run on one RMV fare network; buy a ticket before boarding.
S-Bahn lines S8/S9 link the airport and suburbs; they are often delayed, so allow buffer time.
Single ticket in central Frankfurt is €3.80; a day ticket is €7.75.
Uber, Bolt and Free Now all work in the city.
Driving is easy to reach but parking is hard; use park-and-ride during trade fairs.
The centre is walkable; bikes and e-scooters are widely available.

roemerberg.name: Römerberg
roemerberg.tip: Come early morning for empty photos of the half-timbered houses before the tour groups arrive.

main_tower.name: Main Tower
main_tower.price_text: ≈ EUR 9 for the observation deck; check current price
main_tower.hours: Daily, roughly 10:00–21:00 in summer; check on the day
main_tower.tip: Go up about 30 minutes before sunset to see the skyline in daylight and lit up.

roemer.name: Römer
roemer.price_text: Free to view from outside; city hall inside is not open to tourists
roemer.tip: The three gabled facades are the classic Frankfurt postcard; look up at the small balcony.

goethe_house.name: Goethe House
goethe_house.price_text: ≈ EUR 10 adult; reduced tickets available; check on the day
goethe_house.hours: Daily, usually 10:00–18:00; check on the day
goethe_house.tip: The rebuilt birth house is small; allow an hour and read the room labels for context.

paulskirche.name: St. Paul's Church
paulskirche.tip: This is where Germany's first parliament met in 1848; the round hall is quick to see.

palmengarten.name: Palmengarten
palmengarten.price_text: ≈ EUR 7 adult; check on the day
palmengarten.tip: The glasshouses are great in cold or wet weather; the outdoor gardens need a dry day.

alte_oper.name: Alte Oper
alte_oper.price_text: Concert tickets vary widely; check the programme
alte_oper.hours: Box office and events; check the schedule
alte_oper.tip: Even without a ticket, the square in front is a good evening spot for a drink.

zoo.name: Zoo Frankfurt
zoo.price_text: ≈ EUR 12 adult; check on the day
zoo.tip: Big and spread out; wear comfortable shoes and plan at least half a day.

lochmuehle.name: Freizeitpark Lochmühle
lochmuehle.price_text: ≈ EUR 15 per person; check on the day
lochmuehle.hours: Seasonal, mainly spring to autumn; check opening days
lochmuehle.tip: It is outside the city in the Taunus hills; allow travel time by train and bus.

kleinmarkthalle.name: Kleinmarkthalle
kleinmarkthalle.price_text: Free to enter; food priced per item
kleinmarkthalle.hours: Mon–Fri roughly 08:00–18:00, Sat until about 16:00; closed Sunday
kleinmarkthalle.tip: Grab a sausage or a coffee at a counter for a cheap, local lunch.

eisenerner_steg.name: Eiserner Steg
eisenerner_steg.tip: Walk across at dusk for the best skyline view from the river.

sachsenhausen_walk.name: Sachsenhausen riverside walk
sachsenhausen_walk.tip: Stroll the south bank path and stop at an apple-wine tavern for a local drink.

main_river_cruise.name: Main river sightseeing cruise
main_river_cruise.price_text: ≈ EUR 12–18 for a short city cruise; check on the day
main_river_cruise.tip: Sit on the open deck; a short loop is enough to see the skyline from the water.

bahnhofsviertel_walk.name: Bahnhofsviertel street-food walk
bahnhofsviertel_walk.price_text: Pay per item; budget roughly EUR 10–20
bahnhofsviertel_walk.hours: Best in the evening; many places open late
bahnhofsviertel_walk.tip: The district is gritty but lively; stick to the busy streets and try a kebab or Asian snack.

museumsufer.name: Museumsufer (Museum Embankment)
museumsufer.price_text: Free to walk; museums charge separately, often ≈ EUR 10–12
museumsufer.hours: Promenade always open; museums usually closed Monday
museumsufer.tip: Pick one or two museums rather than trying several; the riverside walk between them is free.

apfelwein_tavern.name: Apple-wine tavern in Sachsenhausen
apfelwein_tavern.hours: Mostly lunch and evening; check on the day
apfelwein_tavern.tip: Order Apfelwein in a traditional ribbed jug and try green sauce with potatoes.

stays.why: Walk to the Römer, cathedral and river in minutes. Quiet at night, few budget rooms.
Cheapest central beds and the main station on your doorstep. Lively and gritty at night.
South-bank Apfelwein taverns and river walks; 10–15 minutes into the centre on foot or tram.
Leafy, calm and close to the trade-fair halls and Palmengarten. Good for business trips.

food: Try Frankfurter Grüne Soße (green herb sauce with eggs and potatoes) and Frankfurter sausages.
Drink Apfelwein (apple wine) in a Sachsenhausen tavern; ask for it 'sauer' with sparkling water.
Kleinmarkthalle market hall: graze on sausages, cheese and coffee, roughly €5–15 per snack.
Bakeries and kiosks sell pretzels and sandwiches for about €3–6; good for a quick lunch.
Book dinner on Friday and Saturday nights; popular taverns fill up. Check prices on the menu first.
more_time: Swap a city afternoon for a Rhine Valley day: trains run south to Rüdesheim and the river villages; check times on the day.
Add a stop at the Städel Museum for old masters and modern art; allow 2–3 hours.
Cross to Sachsenhausen for a slow riverside walk and an Apfelwein dinner instead of a second museum.
